hypothesis: candidate-pool-size confound — the governed multiroute splits requests across OpenAIRE/DBLP/Crossref, many routes return EMPTY/SERVICE_ERROR, yielding smaller pools than the single backend that concentrates all requests on Crossref
finding: Pool-size confound explains much of the gap but not all: single_backend maintains 1-hit advantage even on tasks where both systems have >=50 candidates

strict_hit_at_50.interpretation: BASELINE_AHEAD survives restriction but narrows from 12-hit margin to 1-hit margin

conclusion: The BASELINE_AHEAD negative at hit@50 is partly a candidate-pool artifact: 53% of governed tasks are mechanically capped due to small pools. However, the single backend does maintain a retrieval advantage (1 more hit) even when both systems have >=50 candidates, suggesting a real backend-diversity effect rather than pure pool-size confound.
recommendation: Future head-to-head comparisons should either (a) equalize candidate pools before scoring, or (b) use ranking metrics that are insensitive to absolute pool size (e.g., MRR, precision-recall curves rather than fixed-k cutoffs).
